newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Jan-May consumer prices up 3.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Jan-May consumer prices up 3.1 percent.

text.p: Shanghai's consumer prices rose 3.1 percent in January-May compared with the same period in 1996, the Shanghai Securities News said on Saturday.

Shanghai's retail prices -- a narrower measure of inflation which excludes services -- rose 0.1 percent in the first five months of 1997 compared with the same period in 1996, the newspaper said, quoting the city's statistical bureau.

China's improved economic environment, an ample harvest for Shanghai and the city's own efforts to ensure food supply were responsible for a slowdown in Shanghai's inflation, it said, quoting experts from the bureau.
The experts forecast Shanghai's consumer prices will rise 2.5 percent on the year in the second half of 1997, while retail prices are expected to fall, the newspaper said.
